stats_source: Source: arrival and departure records that GerLines collects from realtime feeds, summed per day and hour.
stats_refreshed_unknown: The time of the last refresh is not known.
stats_lag: Statistics are up to about {minutes} minutes behind the live map.
stats_method_rule: Punctual means an arrival less than 6 minutes late, the rule Deutsche Bahn uses for its published figures. Origins and cancelled stops are not counted. Mean, median and the delay distribution count every observed stop, departures included.
stats_method_gap: For October and November 2025 our figures ran 0.5 to 1.1 points below the monthly figures that Deutsche Bahn publishes.
stats_outside: Not counted: {foreign} stops abroad and {unassigned} stops without a state.
stats_estimated: {count} observed stops use a delay carried over from an earlier report. This leans towards punctual.
stats_category_covers: The headline counts every category above that has data. A category with no data had no observed arrival in this period.
stats_outside_unassigned: Not counted: {unassigned} stops without a state.
stats_line_hint: A line name as shown on the train, for example RE5 or S1.

legal_sources_intro: GerLines shows data from the sources below and derives its own data from them. Each source is listed with its provider, what we use it for, its licence and the credit the licence asks for. We processed, combined and aggregated this data, for example by placing trains on the track and computing delays.
legal_use_delfi_gtfs: Timetable, stops, train numbers and operator names of every train in Germany
legal_use_delfi_realtime: Delays, cancellations, added trains and disruption notices
legal_use_delfi_eva: EVA station numbers that link timetable stops to DB station data
legal_use_vbb: Realtime data for Berlin and Brandenburg
legal_use_vbn: Realtime data for Bremen and Lower Saxony
legal_use_db_timetables: Platforms, station messages and checks of long-distance trains at selected stations
legal_use_db_stada: Station names shown on the site. Lift and escalator status from FaSta is recorded and not shown yet
legal_use_db_open_station: Station infrastructure such as platforms and accessibility
legal_use_db_isr: Infrastructure register. It is paid and only for railway undertakings, so we use OpenStreetMap instead
legal_use_vehicle_sequence: Coach sequence and vehicle series of DB long-distance and DB Regio trains, fetched once per train and day
legal_use_ovapi: Realtime data of trains from the Netherlands
legal_use_czptt: Realtime data and positions of trains from Czechia
legal_use_poland: Realtime data of trains from Poland
legal_use_sncb: Realtime data and notices of trains from Belgium
legal_use_sncf: Realtime data of trains from France
legal_use_switzerland: Realtime data and train formations from Switzerland
legal_use_static_neighbours: Timetables of trains from Austria, Luxembourg and Denmark
legal_use_open_free_map: Base map tiles and the fonts of the map labels
legal_use_planetiler: Our own base map tiles for the public site
legal_use_mapterhorn: Elevation for the Terrain style, its hill shading and 3D terrain
legal_use_bkg_vg250: Outline of Germany, the 16 Länder and the Land focus
legal_use_bkg_places: Towns in search, one point per municipality
legal_use_bkg_towns: The town in the name of each station
legal_use_natural_earth_places: English and Polish names of larger German towns in search
legal_use_osm_rail: Track network that the trains move along
legal_use_bahn_vorhersage_stations: Coordinates of backfilled DB stations the timetable does not know
legal_use_db_punctuality: Checking our punctuality statistics against the figures DB publishes
legal_use_operator_matching: Links from operators to Wikidata for names and logos
legal_use_wikidata: Facts about vehicle series and operators
legal_use_commons: Vehicle photos and some operator logos
legal_use_wikipedia_lines: Which operator and vehicle series usually run on a line
legal_use_wikipedia_series: Vehicle dimensions for the 3D models, facts only
legal_use_data_sheets: Dimensions and car layouts for the 3D models from data sheets, facts only

legal_imagery_intro: The Satellite style shows VersaTiles imagery. For Germany and its neighbours it comes from the providers below, as VersaTiles lists them. Imagery of other areas comes from the other providers on the VersaTiles list.
legal_elevation_intro: The Terrain style and 3D terrain use Mapterhorn elevation tiles. For Germany and its neighbours they are built from the sources below, as Mapterhorn lists them. Other areas use the other sources on the Mapterhorn list.
legal_published_title: What we publish and under which licence
legal_published_intro: Data that we derive from a share-alike source keeps that licence. ODbL 1.0 and CC BY-SA 4.0 ask everyone who reuses it to name the sources, keep the licence and share changed data under the same licence.
legal_published_map: Trains, delays and statistics on the site keep the licence and the credit of each source they come from:
legal_published_map_combined: Train positions are placed along OpenStreetMap tracks and credit OpenStreetMap under ODbL 1.0. Which licence applies where several of these sources are combined is still part of the legal check.
legal_published_shapes: Rail graph and matched train paths: derived from OpenStreetMap, offered under ODbL 1.0 once they are published. They are not published yet.
legal_published_catalogue: Vehicle and operator catalogue: CC BY-SA 4.0 where it draws on Wikipedia, CC0 1.0 for facts from Wikidata and our own choices.
legal_not_affiliated: GerLines is an independent, non-commercial open-source project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by or connected to Deutsche Bahn, DELFI, the Verkehrsverbünde or any railway operator. Names, logos and trademarks belong to their owners and are only used to say who runs a train or provides the data.
legal_not_affiliated_short: Not affiliated with Deutsche Bahn or any operator.
legal_draft_body: This privacy policy is a draft. The owner reviews it and has it checked legally before the site goes public. Parts marked Missing are not filled in yet.
legal_privacy_controller: The controller is the person named in the Impressum. Name, address and contact are added there before the site goes public.
legal_privacy_summary: GerLines has no accounts, sets no cookies and uses no tracking or analytics. You can use every feature without giving us personal data.
legal_privacy_server: Your browser asks our server for the page, the map data and the trains. To answer, the server necessarily receives your IP address and the request. Our server software writes no access log of visitors, and the error messages it writes contain no IP addresses.
legal_privacy_rate_limits: To keep the site available for everyone, our API counts requests per IP address in the memory of the running process: 120 per minute for search, 60 for statistics (10 for long periods), 30 for journeys, 60 punctuality lookups for the trains of journeys, 120 for train details, 120 for train lookups on the map, 60 for the data status and 300 for vehicle photos. An IPv6 address is counted by its first 64 bits, by its first 48 bits while the counter table is full, and by its first 32 bits while a second table is full as well, an IPv4 address then by its first 16. While the coach sequence lookup at bahn.de is switched on, an IP address may also start at most 30 such lookups per hour, an IPv6 address counted by its first 48 bits. A count is removed with the first request after its minute has passed, or its hour for coach sequence lookups, and with every restart. It is never written to disk.
legal_privacy_queries: What you type into search goes to our server with the request. To answer the same search again quickly, the server keeps the typed text and its results in its working memory, without your IP address and never on disk. It reuses them for at most one minute and holds them until 500 newer searches push them out, it builds the search for a new day or timetable, or it restarts. Your browser, and a content delivery network in front of our server once there is one, may keep a search answer for one minute and the details of a station for five minutes. The stations of a journey go to our server and its route planner to answer your request and are not stored. Their answers are sent with the instruction not to keep them. If a journey request fails, the server writes an error line with the error text of the route planner and without your IP address.
legal_privacy_reliability: When the journey planner shows how punctual a train was, your browser sends the category and number of each train of the journeys, with its operator when known, to our server. The server reads their punctuality over the last 30 days from our statistics and keeps the answer per train number in its working memory, without your IP address and never on disk: for at most 10 minutes, for at most 2,000 train numbers with the oldest pushed out first, and never past a restart. Your browser, and a content delivery network in front of our server once there is one, may keep this answer for five minutes.
legal_privacy_hosting: The hosting provider and the content delivery network are not chosen yet. Their names, what they log and how long they keep it are added here before the site goes public.
legal_privacy_storage: The site keeps your choices in the local storage of your browser, so they stay the same on your next visit. It writes a value only when you make that choice, and nothing of it is sent to us. You can delete these values at any time with the site data in your browser settings.
legal_privacy_storage_terrain: The 3D relief of the Terrain map
legal_privacy_storage_buildings: The 3D buildings of the Terrain map
legal_privacy_hosts: Your browser loads parts of the map directly from these hosts. They receive your IP address, the user agent of your browser and the area of the map you look at. Their privacy policies are not linked yet, because we have not checked them.
legal_privacy_host_open_free_map: Base map and the fonts of the map labels, in every map style
legal_privacy_host_versatiles: Imagery, only in the Satellite style
legal_privacy_host_mapterhorn: Elevation, only in the Terrain style
legal_privacy_own_server: The fonts and icons of the interface, the vehicle photos and the 3D models come from our own server. Links to other sites open only when you click them, and they send no referrer.
legal_privacy_basis: Processing your IP address to deliver the site and to limit requests rests on our legitimate interest in a secure and available service (Art. 6 (1) (f) GDPR). Keeping your settings in your browser is strictly necessary for the function you chose (§ 25 (2) no. 2 TDDDG).
legal_privacy_retention: Request counts: at most until the first request after their minute, or their hour for coach sequence lookups, and never past a restart. Search texts in server memory: reused for at most one minute and held until 500 newer searches push them out, a new day or timetable comes, or the server restarts. Train numbers of punctuality lookups in server memory: at most 10 minutes, at most 2,000 of them, and never past a restart. Search answers in your browser: one minute, station details and punctuality answers five minutes. Settings in your browser: until you delete them. Logs of the hosting provider: missing until it is chosen.
legal_privacy_rights: You have the right of access, rectification, erasure, restriction of processing and objection, and the right to lodge a complaint with a data protection supervisory authority (Art. 15 to 21 and 77 GDPR). Write to the contact in the Impressum.
legal_privacy_planned: Visitor statistics with Umami, without cookies, are planned for the launch and are not built yet. This policy is updated before they start.
legal_imprint_draft: The owner has not added these details yet. The site does not go public before they are filled in and checked legally.
legal_imprint_responsible: Responsible for the content under § 18 (2) MStV
predict_note: Forecast, not measured. From runs {from} to {to} that left a stop in the same delay range as this train, on time, 1 to 5, 6 to 15 or over 15 minutes late: the typical arrival delay, and the delay that 8 in 10 of those runs stayed under.
predict_attribution_piebro: Deutsche Bahn train data, collected and processed by piebro, data from Deutsche Bahn
predict_method: Method B1, historical quantiles, shown where it beat the current delay carried forward in the backtest.
profile_error: The profile could not be loaded.
profile_empty: No segments of this train in this period.
profile_not_placed: The profile cannot be placed on the route drawn for this run, so it is not shown on the map.
profile_legend_title: Delay gain of this train against all trains
profile_curtain: Curtain height: minutes this train loses on the segment, up to {cap}
profile_reason_too_few: Too few runs: {runs}, at least {min} are needed
profile_reason_not_in_profile: This leg is not in the profile of the period
profile_note: Delay gain is the delay at the end of a segment minus the delay at its start, in whole minutes. Positive means time lost. Many legs show exactly 0, because feeds report whole minutes and legs after a feed stopped reporting keep a gain of 0.

match.countPlural=one: {count} segment of this route is in the data under another station id, so it shows no figures here
match.countPlural=other: {count} segments of this route are in the data under other station ids, so they show no figures here

predict_title_feed: Forecast with a range from history
predict_spread_train: Live forecast, spread of this train
predict_spread_stop: Live forecast, spread of trains of this kind here
predict_spread_category: Live forecast, spread of trains of this kind
predict_note_feed: Forecast, not measured. The typical value is the arrival delay the live data from {feed} predicts for the stop. The 8 in 10 bound adds the spread of runs {from} to {to} that left a stop in the same delay range as this train, on time, 1 to 5, 6 to 15 or over 15 minutes late: the gap between their typical arrival delay and the delay that 8 in 10 of them stayed under.
predict_note_rest: At stops without a live forecast, both values come from those runs.
predict_method_feed: The live forecast is shown where the feed has one, as it came closer than method B1 in a live check. Spread from method B1, historical quantiles.

status_not_configured: The status server is not set up.
status_live_none: The live map sends no updates
status_live_no_reading: No reading of the live map
status_note: Up to date means the newest data is within the limit of its source, {min} to {max} minutes. Data is stale means it is older than that limit. Down means no new data for an hour, or a source that is not fetched. Not recorded means no data of the source is held. Timetables change only when they are published.

playback_error_unreadable: The data of this hour cannot be read.
